key_insight: Serum brain-derived tau (BD-tau) distinguished traumatic brain injury (TBI) from spinal cord injury (SCI), supporting its potential as an injury-specific blood biomarker.
clinical_relevance: If validated, serum BD-tau could support acute neurotrauma differentiation, triage, and injury-specific trial enrollment; this study concerns neurotrauma, not AI cancer drug discovery.
method: Multi-cohort assessment of 285 patients with TBI, 57 with SCI, and 22 controls.
Compared serum BD-tau with paired cerebrospinal fluid measurements and established blood biomarkers.
Tracked serum BD-tau trajectories through 144 hours after injury.
evidence_signal: Serum BD-tau distinguished TBI from SCI with AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.96) overall and outperformed comparator blood biomarkers in a separate reported comparison (AUC 0.82 versus 0.53–0.71; all DeLong p<0.001).
watch_item: The abstract does not establish clinical decision thresholds or performance in mixed TBI–SCI presentations, requiring further validation before routine use.
paper_title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
